# Finding families

Every graded finding carries a stable, dotted `family.item` code (charter koan 9, *errors are lore*). The code is the contract a benchmark, a repair tool, or a downstream consumer matches on — it is stable across message wording. This page catalogues every code the system emits: its family (the check or tool that raises it), its severity, the machine-repair kind it carries (Door-T authoring findings only), and what it means.

These finding codes are **disjoint** from the wire error-code registry (the 13 `ErrorCode` values in `error-codes.md`, per the dli-worker contract §3.2 / §9). The distinction is load-bearing: a wire error code says the *call* failed — it was malformed (`schema`), refused by principle (`refused`), or hit a server defect (`internal`); a finding code is a graded *domain* observation about the lore itself. A well-formed call over inconsistent lore returns findings, not an error. No code appears in both sets.

**128 codes** across **10 families** (plus the `proof.resource-violation` sub-codes). A `family.item` code names its check battery in the family and the specific violation in the item. Two codes can share a stem across families — the naming vet's `name.register-fit` (a kernel warn) and Door T's `name.unvetted` (an authoring warn) are different findings from different surfaces.


> Note: severity is a property of the emitting site. Kernel check findings (`load`, `continuity`, `proof`, `practice`, `attest`, `name`, `citation`) carry no machine repair — read the message. Only the Door-T `author.*` findings carry structured repairs, which is what makes `author.materialize` gateable.

## load — the loader's fail-closed gate

- **Emitted by:** the world loader, run by `deloreis check` / `dli.check` before any query
- **Owner:** `dli-world :: model.rs (LoadFinding)`
- **Severity:** All error: a load finding holds its declaration fail-closed — unassertable until fixed. Fail-closed provenance *is* the assertability gate.

| Code | Severity | Repair | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `load.missing-provenance` | error | — | a declaration carries no ruling and no hypothesis, so it cannot be asserted. |
| `load.malformed-provenance` | error | — | the provenance annotation cannot be read; held fail-closed until the annotation is fixed. |
| `load.malformed-world-rule` | error | — | a bare top-level world rule is not valid Datalog and is refused instead of lowering no rule. |
| `load.unbound-head-variable` | error | — | a rule concludes about a variable that nothing in its premises names. |
| `load.duplicate-declaration` | error | — | a name is declared twice as the same kind within one scope. |
| `load.cross-pack-collision` | error | — | a name is declared in more than one scope/pack. |
| `load.unstratifiable` | error | — | the rules cannot be ordered for evaluation — a negative-dependency cycle (FRONT-1). |

## continuity — the world-consistency battery

- **Emitted by:** the continuity checks, run by `dli.check` (world-internal) and `check-draft` (claim-relative)
- **Owner:** `dli-world :: check/continuity.rs (WorldFinding)`
- **Severity:** All error: a continuity finding is a contradiction of canon or an assertion the claim may not make.

| Code | Severity | Repair | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `continuity.chronology-cycle` | error | — | the before-graph closes a cycle; the timeline would have no consistent order. |
| `continuity.prior-contradiction` | error | — | a claim contradicts an established prior certain fact. |
| `continuity.rejected-lore` | error | — | a certain fact realizes a killed/rejected token. |
| `continuity.unknown-entity` | error | — | a claim references an entity that is not in scope. |
| `continuity.proposed-as-fact` | error | — | a claim states shadow (proposed) lore as settled. |
| `continuity.intra-episode-contradiction` | error | — | a claim set fixes one slot two contradictory ways within an episode. |

## name — the naming-oracle kernel vet

- **Emitted by:** the world-true half of the naming oracle, run by `dli.name.check` and the language layer of `check`
- **Owner:** `dli-world :: language/derivation.rs (LangFinding)`
- **Severity:** Warn: a name defect warns rather than blocks (grade `checked`); the factory-side world-safe screens live outside the kernel. (Distinct from the Door-T `name.unvetted` finding below.)

| Code | Severity | Repair | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name.slot-sequence` | warn | — | the name's slots match no name-kind pattern of its dialect. |
| `name.role-membership` | warn | — | a name-part is not declared in the dialect under the role it fills. |
| `name.register-fit` | warn | — | the name does not fit its declared dialect/register. |
| `name.phonotactics` | warn | — | the name violates the dialect's phonotactics (vowels, endings, clusters, stress). |
| `name.uniqueness` | warn | — | the name collides with an existing name in canon. |
| `name.fixed-token-reuse` | warn | — | the name reuses a fixed token reserved elsewhere. |
| `name.aural-clash` | warn | — | the name is aurally too close to another across the whole name-space. |
| `name.set-clash` | warn | — | the name is not aurally distinct within its declared set. |
| `name.gender-morphology` | warn | — | the name's morphology conflicts with its declared gender. |
| `name.sayability-cap` | warn | — | the name exceeds the sayability-tier caps (D-0095). |
| `name.banned-in-name` | warn | — | the name realizes banned diegetic vocabulary. |
| `name.confusable` | warn | — | the id mixes a Latin-looking form with a look-alike character from another script (a homoglyph). |

## attest — the attestation seam

- **Emitted by:** the attestation lookup a check consumes, surfaced as `dli.attest.missing`
- **Owner:** `dli-world :: attest.rs (AttestFinding)`
- **Severity:** Error for the consuming check: the kernel reads what a sweep committed and never fabricates a judgment, so an absent record stops the check rather than guessing an answer.

| Code | Severity | Repair | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `attest.missing` | error | — | the question has no attestation in the store; a sweep must pose it before a check can consume it. |

## practice — practice well-formedness

- **Emitted by:** the practice-block checker, run by `deloreis check` / `dli.check` when a `practice` is declared
- **Owner:** `dli-ledger :: practice.rs (PracticeFinding)`
- **Severity:** Error: a malformed practice cannot host a proof, so each finding blocks the practice.

| Code | Severity | Repair | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `practice.error-refines-nothing` | error | — | a declared error refines a token that is not one of the seven structural classes L1–L7. |
| `practice.missing-discriminant` | error | — | two errors share a structural class with no discriminant to tell them apart. |
| `practice.resource-outside-algebra` | error | — | a resource's declared law is outside the closed resource algebra. |
| `practice.unbound-sort` | error | — | a role is typed by a sort the practice does not declare, that is not a primitive kind or an in-scope cycle. |
| `practice.unresolved-cycle` | error | — | a failure or law cites a cycle that is not in scope. |
| `practice.error-resource-unknown` | error | — | an L6 resource-violation error spends against a resource the practice does not declare. |
| `practice.renamed-interior-form` | error | — | a practice interior wrote a retired spelling (a killed form); refused with its successor named. |

## proof — the diegetic proof checker

- **Emitted by:** the proof/ledger checker, run by `deloreis check-proof` / `dli.check-proof`
- **Owner:** `dli-ledger :: ledger_check.rs (ProofFinding)`
- **Severity:** Error: a proof finding means the spoken proof is invalid; the L-class in the message (L1–L7) names which structural obligation broke.

| Code | Severity | Repair | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `proof.unknown-form` | error | — | the form is not declared by this practice (L1). |
| `proof.premise-absent` | error | — | a premise is not established in the scene — the casting fizzles (L2, absent). |
| `proof.premise-contradicted` | error | — | a premise is denied by the certain projection — the casting rebounds (L2, contradicted). |
| `proof.wrong-phase` | error | — | a step runs at the wrong cyclic phase (L3, timing). |
| `proof.bad-instantiation` | error | — | a form is instantiated with ill-typed arguments (L4). |
| `proof.invalid-chain` | error | — | a chain step does not follow from its cited premises (L5). |
| `proof.resource-violation` | error | — | the ledger breaches a resource law (L6) — see the resource sub-codes below. |
| `proof.close-mismatch` | error | — | the close atom does not match what the steps derived (L7). |
| `proof.expectation-unmet` | error | — | the proof's expected verdict was not met (the expected-verdict discipline). |
| `proof.invalid-spend` | error | — | a spend draws against a resource illegally. |
| `proof.unknown-spoke` | error | — | a step cites a spoke or label that the proof does not define. |
| `proof.unknown-expectation` | error | — | an expectation names something the practice does not define. |
| `proof.missing-close` | error | — | the proof has no close step. |
| `proof.practice-mismatch` | error | — | the proof's `in <practice>` clause does not match the practice being checked. |

## resource — the discriminants of proof.resource-violation

- **Emitted by:** the resource-algebra accounting inside the proof checker; carried as the discriminant of `proof.resource-violation`
- **Owner:** `dli-ledger :: resource.rs (ResourceViolationCode)`
- **Severity:** Sub-codes, not standalone families: each names how a `proof.resource-violation` breached the closed algebra.

| Code | Severity | Repair | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `overspent` | error | — | a linear or affine balance fell below zero — a unit was spent that was never accounted. |
| `over-capacity` | error | — | an affine balance rose above its declared capacity. |
| `not-conserved` | error | — | a `linear conserved` multiset did not net to zero at the close — a step minted or burned it. |
| `wrong-direction` | error | — | a graded-monotone grade moved against its one declared direction. |

## citation — lowering findings

- **Emitted by:** the evaluator's lowering pass, surfaced through `check`
- **Owner:** `dli-eval :: world.rs (LowerFinding)`
- **Severity:** Warn (non-fatal): lowering never aborts on one — it fails the affected claim closed and records the finding so the rest of the world still checks.

| Code | Severity | Repair | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `citation.unknown-decision` | warn | — | a claim cites a decision the corpus never declares; the claim is failed closed. |

## author — Door-T authoring findings

- **Emitted by:** the `author.*` MCP tools (Door T)
- **Owner:** `dli-serve :: author/tools.rs (Finding)`
- **Severity:** Per-code severity gates `author.materialize`: an `error` blocks it, a `warn` passes. These are the findings that carry structured machine repairs.

| Code | Severity | Repair | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name.unvetted` | warn | `run-check` | a name has not passed the naming oracle; it enters proposed and unvetted. |
| `entity.unknown` | error | `resolve-entity` | no entity of that id is in scope; the claim is staged but cannot materialize until it exists. |
| `event.era-missing` | error | — | an event has no era anchor; every event must occur during a declared era. |
| `event.era-kind` | error | — | an event's era anchor names an entity that is not an era. |
| `fact.contradiction` | error | — | a claimed slot value contradicts a certain fact the base asserts. |
| `order.cycle` | error | — | a `before` fact would close a cycle against the existing orderings. |
| `consequence.changed` | warn | — | under a supposition the derived-consequence set may move; see `author.diff`. |
| `hypothesis.not-in-fork` | error | — | a hypothesis is legal only in a fork workspace. |
| `hypothesis.bundle-limit` | error | — | a proposal bundle carries at most one hypothesis; a second supposition is a second fork. |
| `hypothesis.unknown` | error | — | no hypothesis of that id is staged in this workspace to suppose. |
| `question.unknown` | error | — | no open question of that id exists in this workspace to add an option to. |
| `field.control-char` | error | `remove-control-chars` | a free-text field carries a control/bidi/zero-width character that could forge or reorder a declaration in the review diff. |
| `provenance.cited-refused` | error | `add-provenance` | Door T authors `proposed` or `hypothesis` only; an agent cannot cite a ruling to mint canon authority. |

## craft — the season-ledger join-rule battery

- **Emitted by:** `check_season_rules` / `check_episode` in `dli-world::craft::season` (CRAFT-2)
- **Owner:** `dli-world :: craft/season.rs + craft/kb.rs (WorldFinding, via KernelRule)`
- **Severity:** Mixed error/warn per rule: structural verdicts (accomplishment-earned, yes-and-terminal, scene-name-clash) are error; band/threshold rules are warn until calibrated. This lane is landing under CRAFT-2; covered by a no-phantom check.

| Code | Severity | Repair | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `craft.accomplishment-earned` | error | — | a major beat needs a prior same-thread failure; the triumph is unearned. |
| `craft.accomplishment-earned-climax` | warn | — | a climax-class beat needs two prior failures; the climax rests on too few. |
| `craft.yes-and-terminal` | error | — | a thread re-opens after its unqualified win; a yes-and is terminal per thread. |
| `craft.competence-consistency` | warn | — | an unearned major win by an under-competent hand with no intervening growth. |
| `craft.competence-arc-flat` | warn | — | competence never moves across the season; the character does not grow. |
| `craft.reveal-fair-play` | warn | — | a turn's reframing fact is not on the listener ledger early enough (kishōtenketsu fair-play). |
| `craft.mystery-starved` | warn | — | a mystery promise goes untouched for too many consecutive episodes. |
| `craft.cold-open-discipline` | warn | — | cold-open discipline: open a loop, cast within ceiling, no deep-time in act 1. |
| `craft.cast-introduction-rate` | warn | — | new named speakers per episode exceed the band or the season budget. |
| `craft.scene-name-clash` | error | — | two names below the aural-distinctness floor share a scene. |
| `craft.promise-density` | warn | — | promise open/close density violates the season-position bands. |
| `craft.arc-shape` | warn | — | a kishōtenketsu episode places its ten out of band or resolves a conflict. |
| `craft.audio-load-trajectory` | warn | — | too many consecutive high-orientation-load episodes without recovery. |
